key_insight: The study combines ordinal diagnosis prediction, multi-horizon trajectory forecasting, and uncertainty decomposition to better model how Alzheimer's disease progresses over time.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help clinicians interpret not only the most likely next diagnosis, but also how reliably a patient’s future cognitive and biomarker changes are predicted.
method: Temporal Fusion Transformer encoder + CORAL ordinal output for next-visit diagnosis prediction
Autoregressive Mixture Density Network to generate 5-year probabilistic trajectories for diagnosis, CDR-SB, MMSE orientation, and hippocampal volume
Bootstrap ensemble plus analytic mixture variance to separate epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty
evidence_signal: On ADNI, the model outperformed linear, recurrent, and transformer baselines for next-visit diagnosis prediction, achieved near-nominal 90% credible interval coverage, and showed increased epistemic uncertainty on external OASIS-3 evaluation.
watch_item: Performance and uncertainty estimates may be less stable for rare progression patterns and across external datasets, so real-world deployment would need careful validation and calibration.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Longitudinal Forecasting of Alzheimer's Disease Progression Using Deep Learning
